account:
Today has mostly followed my appointment book: morning office business, a ten o'clock visit to the mill, and noon at home. I am now due back at the office at thirteen for council letters, then tea with the neighbour at fifteen. The secretary supplied the appointment book this morning and reported no new council letters or requests. The filed books have not otherwise been verified.

The unusual matter is repeated, very vague talk of a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery and inn. Townsfolk 11 and 02 repeated it near the mill. Townsfolk 01 associated the bakery report with the baker, freight and neighbour, but gave no concrete description of any change. I asked what actually happened and who first reported it; I have not received a substantive answer. I have seen no alteration myself, so I cannot tell whether this refers to a proposal, actual work, or merely circulating gossip, nor what it is intended for.

The miller was also absent when I visited for the grain inspection. The baker had already said that he could not find the miller this morning. I called for the miller and requested stock figures and delivery records, but did not locate either the miller or those records. The scheduled visit was made, but the inspection remains incomplete; I have no evidence explaining the absence.

The builder asked for jobs earlier, but I have no confirmed damage and have authorized no paid inspections, repairs or spending. The baker asked about gatherings needing bread; neither the secretary nor I had a confirmed public gathering or bread order. My afternoon tea is private, not a town catering request. Nothing I have learned yet establishes a connection between these routine inquiries and the bridge or port rumours.
